findings.title: Migration crashes when the embed_category site setting row is missing or unmatched
findings.body: The migration computes the default category with `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. site_settings only contains rows for settings an admin explicitly changed, and `embed_category` defaulted to blank, so for the vast majority of installations (and every fresh install) this query returns zero rows. Indexing `[0]` on an empty result set returns nil (or raises IndexError depending on the pg adapter version), so `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError and the entire migration aborts, blocking the upgrade. The fallback for `category_id == 0` on line 15 (`... WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value']`) has the same problem if that row is absent. Both lookups need to tolerate an empty result (e.g. `.first` with a nil check or a begin/rescue) before dereferencing.

findings.title: Legacy host values are inserted raw and may silently stop matching after migration
findings.body: The migration copies values from the legacy `embeddable_hosts` setting straight into the new table with `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. The old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` stripped `http(s)://` prefixes when matching (and the old specs explicitly covered scheme-prefixed entries working), but `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares the bare hostname (`uri.host`) against the stored value with `lower(host) = ?`. The model strips schemes/paths in `before_validation`, but the migration bypasses the model, so any legacy entries stored as `http://example.com`, with paths, uppercase, or trailing `\r` from Windows line endings will be inserted verbatim and will never match again — embedding silently breaks for those sites. Additionally the value is interpolated directly into the SQL string, so a host containing a single quote produces invalid SQL and fails the migration; values should be normalized and passed through quoting/bound parameters.

findings.title: update and destroy 500 on an unknown host id instead of returning 404
findings.body: `update` does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and passes the result to `save_host`, which immediately calls `host.host = ...`; `destroy` calls `host.destroy`. If the id does not exist (stale page, deleted host, scripted request), `host` is nil and both actions raise NoMethodError, returning a 500. Other admin controllers in the codebase handle this by raising Discourse::NotFound (404); these actions should do the same.

findings.title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: The `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. If a record is built without a host (for example an admin API request missing `embeddable_host[host]`, which `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns without a presence check), `sub!` is invoked on nil and raises NoMethodError, turning what should be a validation failure into a 500. Guard with `if self.host.present?` (or use non-mutating `sub` after a nil check) and add `validates_presence_of :host`.

findings.title: Host validation accepts ports but record lookup can never match them
findings.body: The validation regex `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i` explicitly permits an optional `:port` suffix, so an admin can successfully save `example.com:3000`. However `record_for_host` compares `uri.host` — which never includes the port — against the stored value, so a host saved with a port will never match and embedding from it will always be rejected. Either strip the port in `before_validation` like the scheme/path are stripped, or disallow it in the regex.

findings.title: Host regex rejects valid TLDs longer than 5 characters
findings.body: The TLD portion of the validation regex is `[a-z]{2,5}`, which rejects real domains under longer TLDs such as `.museum`, `.travel`, or `.technology`. The previous free-form site setting accepted these hosts, so sites embedding from such domains can no longer add them through the new admin UI. The TLD segment should allow a more generous length (e.g. `{2,}`).

findings.title: New host saved without choosing a category shows a blank category until reload
findings.body: In the `save` action, after the record is created the component runs `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`. For a newly added host the `categoryId` property starts as null (the user is not required to pick a category; the server substitutes `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`), so `findById(null)` returns undefined and the row's category badge renders blank even though the server assigned the uncategorized category. The correct category only appears after a full page reload. The component should resolve the category from the category_id returned in the save response when `categoryId` is unset.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents were swapped
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) were moved into `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. The suite still loads because Fabrication reads every file in the directory, but the fabricators live in files with the wrong names, which will confuse future maintainers; the contents should be swapped so each fabricator lives in its namesake file.

findings.title: New admin controllers have no request-level specs
findings.body: Both new controller specs (`admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`) only assert that the controller is a subclass of Admin::AdminController. There is no coverage for create/update/destroy behavior, validation errors, the category defaulting to uncategorized, or the unknown-id case — which is how the nil-host NoMethodError in `update`/`destroy` slips through. At minimum, request specs exercising the happy paths and the missing-record paths should be added.
